A.explanation: An $\alpha$-particle removes $4$ from $A$ and $2$ from $Z$, so $^{226}_{88}\text{Ra}$ should give $A = 222$, not $A = 224$.

B.explanation: An $\alpha$-decay cannot increase $A$ from $238$ to $242$ and $Z$ from $92$ to $94$ because the emitted particle carries away nucleons and charge.

C.explanation: A $\beta^-$-decay keeps $A$ at $228$ but increases $Z$ by $1$ to $89$, so $^{228}_{87}\text{Fr}$ with $Z = 87$ cannot be formed.

D.explanation: A $\beta^-$-decay leaves $A = 231$ unchanged and increases $Z$ from $90$ to $91$, which exactly matches $^{231}_{91}\text{Pa}$.

hints: Look at the top nucleon number $A$ and bottom proton number $Z$ for the parent and product in each row of the table.
Recall that $\alpha$ gives $A-4$ and $Z-2$, while $\beta^-$ gives $A$ unchanged and $Z+1$ because a neutron changes to a proton.
Test each row by subtracting or adding those amounts and keep the row where both $A$ and $Z$ of the product match exactly.
walkthrough: Identify $A$ on top and $Z$ on the bottom: for example row D is $^{231}_{90}\text{Th}$ decaying to $^{231}_{91}\text{Pa}$.
State the conservation rules: $\alpha = ^{4}_{2}\text{He}$ so $A \to A-4$ and $Z \to Z-2$; $\beta^-$ is a neutron to proton change so $A \to A$ and $Z \to Z+1$.
Check the $\alpha$ rows: row A predicts $226-4 = 222$, not $224$, and row B predicts decreases in $A$ and $Z$, not increases to $242$ and $94$.
Check the $\beta^-$ rows: row C predicts $Z = 88+1 = 89$, not $87$, while row D predicts $A = 231$ and $Z = 90+1 = 91$.
Only the $^{231}_{90}\text{Th}$ to $^{231}_{91}\text{Pa}$ $\beta^-$ change conserves both nucleon number and charge. This is option D.
